page: Amazon Web Services i7i.48xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 8559C processors built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 192 virtual CPUs, corresponding to 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The processor configuration includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is a primary feature of this instance, consisting of 45,000 GB of bundled NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the i7i.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and database operations. The server achieved top-tier status in multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU scores, and Redis SET operations, where it sustained 205.98 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds exceeding 13,280 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds reaching 238.51 GB/sec. However, single-core performance sits in the average tier, indicating that workloads must be highly parallelized to fully exploit the hardware capabilities.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density of 192 vCPUs combined with 45 TB of local NVMe SSD storage reduces the need for external block storage attachments, optimizing the cost-per-gigabyte ratio for data-intensive deployments. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions also enables strong performance in specialized tasks like software compilation and large-model LLM inference prompt processing. This configuration is highly suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, data warehousing, and parallelized analytics pipelines.
